title: instrument-gpu-energy-rollup-and-invocation-weighted-alerting
author: Anika Shah
release_notes: Adds GPU power and per-invocation energy rollups; introduces an energy-aware alert weighting policy and a dashboard for energy vs latency/cost analysis.
description: Motivation: As customers optimize inference costs they increasingly ask for power/energy visibility (for cloud cost modeling and on-prem power budgeting). This PR instruments GPU power telemetry, synthesizes per-invocation energy rollups, and exposes a dashboard + alert-weighting policy so SRE and platform teams can reason about energy vs latency/cost tradeoffs. Summary of changes: 1) runtime: hook into the GPU power telemetry provider (nVML/k8s metrics) and emit a new timeseries 'gpu.power.watts' tagged by host, gpu_uuid, model, and instance; 2) aggregator: add a lightweight invocation energy estimator that integrates per-token GPU power over invocation duration to produce invocation_energy_joules and token_energy_joules metrics; 3) metrics pipeline: introduce rollup jobs that produce hourly/day summaries per-tenant and per-model (avg, p50/p95/p99 energy per-invocation); 4) alerting: add 'energy-weighted-alerts' policy which scales alert severity by a normalized invocation_energy_joules * token_cost, reducing noisy low-impact triggers; 5) dashboard: new 'Energy vs Latency & Cost' dashboard with panels for per-GPU power heatmaps, invocation energy distribution, and correlation scatterplots (energy vs latency, energy vs token-cost); 6) tests: unit tests for the estimator and integration tests that validate low overhead and correct tag propagation. Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached: https://linear.app/redwood/eng/ENG-1823-gpu-energy-observability (internal) - [x] Implementation of nVML integration with fallback to Prometheus node-exporter metrics - [x] Unit tests (estimator, tag propagation) - [x] End-to-end bench verifying <2% tail latency regression - [x] Dashboard JSON and alert rules added - [x] Documentation snippet for operators and upgrade notes - [x] Security review for telemetry labels Commits (high-level): - 5b2c3a4: add nVML power reader + feature flag - c7e9e21: implement invocation energy estimator and per-token attribution - 1a4d0ff: metrics rollup jobs and TTLs; add tenant-level summaries - 9d7b8a2: dashboards and alert rules + doc updates - f2c1e9b: tests and CI flake fixes Changed top-level areas (high level listing, not exhaustive): - runtime/gpu_power/ (new) - telemetry/metrics/energy_estimator.py - telemetry/rollups/energy_rollup_job.py - observability/dashboards/energy_vs_latency.json - observability/alerts/energy_weighted_rules.yaml - docs/observability/energy_metrics.md - tests/telemetry/test_energy_estimator.py - tests/integration/test_energy_end2end.py - scripts/bench/energy_overhead_bench.sh - deployments/k8s/metrics-service.yaml Review conversation (selected highlights, chronological): - Marcus Li (2024-11-08): "Nice work — can you confirm what the sampling rate is for polling GPU power and how that impacts estimation accuracy? Also, please ensure we don't expose internal hostnames in tenant-scoped metrics." - Author (Anika) (2024-11-08): "We poll at 200ms when an invocation is active and 1s otherwise; estimator uses linear interpolation between samples. Hostnames are sanitized before emitting tenant-level rollups (we only keep gpu_uuid and region). Added a note in the docs." - Priya Nair (2024-11-09): "Alert weighting idea is compelling, but I'd like to see a short historical calibration step (30d) default to avoid accidental suppression of important alerts." - Author (Anika) (2024-11-09): "Added a calibration window and a conservative default (energy_weight_factor=0.5) with operator override in UIS. See observability/alerts/README.md for tuning guidance." - David Ko (2024-11-10): "What about customers who don't run our metrics daemon (on-prem)? Can the estimator fall back to modeled power based on GPU SKU?" - Author (Anika) (2024-11-10): "Yes: implemented a SKU-based fallback that uses a small interpolation table with measured baselines and annotated confidence scores in the rollups." - Marcus Li (2024-11-11): "CI flake on integration test fixed; re-running." CI summary: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests: pass (including e2e bench that validates <2% median latency overhead) - Lint: pass - Security scan: pass Performance/overhead: Microbench on a 4xA100 node with 200 concurrent short invocations shows median added CPU <0.8% and median latency delta 0.9% at p50, p95 delta 1.6% — within the team target. Observability artifacts: - New metrics documented: 'gpu.power.watts' (gauge), 'invocation_energy_joules' (counter/rollup), 'token_energy_joules' (gauge histogram). - Labeling: model, tenant_id, region, gpu_uuid, instance_type, invocation_phase (decode/encode/kv-cache). - Dashboard: energy_vs_latency.json added to observability dashboards with example panels and drilldowns. Alerting: - energy_weighted_rules.yaml provides a rule that multiplies conventional error/latency SLO signal by a normalized energy factor and then applies the existing alert bucketing. Defaults conservative; operators can opt-out. Migration/upgrade notes: - Feature gated: OFF by default. Enable via config flag 'observability.enable_gpu_energy'. - For on-prem: operators must ensure metrics-daemon provides power metrics or enable SKU fallback. - Rollout plan: canary on dedicated clusters for 1 week, then gradual ramps. Documentation: docs/observability/energy_metrics.md includes explanation, tuning guidance, and FAQs. Merge outcome: approved by Marcus Li on 2024-11-12 and merged via squash. Post-merge actions: - Monitor energy dashboards for first 72 hours - Notify platform customers in the next release notes - Follow-up ticket created to evaluate adding per-session energy cap alerts: ENG-1880 Notes on uniqueness/why this is different: Most prior PRs focus on token-cost, latency distributions, or span sampling. This change explicitly correlates power telemetry with invocation token-level estimates to enable energy-aware platform decisions and alert de-noising based on impact. It introduces a cross-cutting estimator that sits between runtime and metrics pipeline and is intentionally lightweight to limit runtime impact.
notes: Canary rollout scheduled; onboarded to release v0.42.1
